rows.secondDefectFoundWhileRepairing: The composed-page renderer wrapped against MAX_WIDTH using font.widthOfTextAtSize, which is a sum of AFM ADVANCE widths and not the extent of the ink a renderer lays down. Measured here at 300 dpi: five of the eighteen delivered canonical pages already had rendered ink past the declared 552pt right edge of the text box, worst 552.96pt. One of this lane's rewritten motion-page-1 lines measured 491.867pt against a 492pt box - 0.13pt of headroom - and drew ink to 554.88pt, 2.88pt outside it. Inside the paper and inside every clipping margin, but the build was asserting a box it was not holding. A WRAP_SAFETY of 8pt now separates the wrap width from the asserted width, so the two cannot drift apart silently. After the change, zero pages on either fixture carry rendered ink past 552pt and the smallest right gutter on any page is 64.80pt, against 57.1pt before.

rows.whatWasWrong: The packet wrote the participant's name onto the HCJDC 159(b) application in the wrong order, on all five routes and both fixtures, and told the participant nothing about it. The Data Center's printed caption is 'Current Legal Name (Last, First, Middle):' - surname first. The delivered ink was 'Jordan Avery Reyes' on canonical and 'Kahealani Mahealani Kealohilani-Nakamura' on boundary, given name first, so the application told the Data Center the applicant's surname was Jordan, or Kahealani, on the form it uses to find the record in the statewide repository. No counter could see it: the field map held the true caption twice, as printedTextAtCoordinate and printedCaptionOnTheOfficialForm, but printedLabel, effectiveLabel and regionHeading were all reduced to 'Current legal name' with the format instruction stripped, and classifyField and classifyBlank read the reduced label.
rows.whyItWasNotFixedByReorderingTheName: The platform holds the name only as the single string participant.full_legal_name. There is no surname or given-name split anywhere in the builder. Deriving 'Reyes, Jordan Avery' from 'Jordan Avery Reyes' is a guess about which token is the surname, and on the boundary fixture - Kahealani Mahealani Kealohilani-Nakamura - the guess is exactly the kind that would put the wrong surname on a repository search. A value may be prefilled only if the packet actually knows it. This packet does not know it, so the line is now a labelled blank with an instruction.

rows.whyThisLaneStopped: Repairing ROUTE_OPTIONS here means choosing between two rules of the completeness contract on a sworn petition, and this lane holds neither the determination nor the facts to choose. FIX105 withdrew the `guilty` election deliberately, under the row-integrity rule that an election is a member of the row it states: NJ_PETITION_CONVICTION_ROW declares nine cells and six of them - guiltyStatute, guiltyFinal1, guiltyTimeType, guiltyDocCmpltDt, guiltyProbDt, guiltyFineDt - have no mapped fact and are REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, so the row is withheld whole and its election with it. Marking the box while the paragraph it belongs to is blank would put a pre-ticked assertion of a guilty plea on a document sworn by the participant. Supplying the six cells instead needs fact descriptors the platform does not hold. Either route is a legal determination plus a product change, not a KNOWN_PREFILLS repair, and VF11 expressly declined to propose the remedy. Nothing was changed.
exactlyWhatIsMissing: A determination, from counsel or from the owner of the completeness contract, on whether a route-determined election box may be marked on Form A item (d) while the cells of that paragraph are left as REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING blanks - that is, whether ROUTE_OPTIONS or the repeating-row integrity rule governs when they conflict on a sworn petition.

If the answer is that the row must be complete before the box is marked: held fact descriptors for the six unmapped cells of Form A item (d) - the statute of conviction, the final sentence, the type of incarceration, the date incarceration was completed, the date probation was completed and the date the fines were paid. The platform holds none of them today.
